newsitem.title: USA: W. African crudes plentiful on U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: W. African crudes plentiful on U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast refiners continued to enjoy a wide selection of West African crudes on Friday, although demand was limited, traders said.
Most traders blamed the heavy influx on European and Far Eastern refiners' weak appetites.
One East Coast trader also reported a problem at a Gulf Coast refinery which in turn was backing West African crude into the market.
The report could not be confirmed.
Cabinda was assessed at the equivalent to Dated Brent minus 1.25-50 a barrel fob, loading in March.
Bonny Light and Qua Iboe were at the equivalent of around Dated Brent plus 35-45 cents a barrel for March loading.

North Sea barrels remained scarce on the Gulf Coast, reflecting the narrowing spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent. The gap was around $1.40-45 a barrel Friday afternoon, rendering transatlantic trade uneconomic.
Swiss-based trading house Glencore continued to gobble up Brent cargoes, picking up a March 16-18 and a March 17-19 for April Brent plus 25 cents a barrel each.
On the Latin American scene, traders noted a continued abundance of Colombian Cano Limon. The grade was offered at a discount of $2.50 a barrel under WTI.
Colombian Vasconia was assessed at around WTI minus $3.30 a barrel.
Elsewhere, Uruguay's 37,000 barrel per day (bpd) La Teja refinery is due back on stream in the second or third week of March after a maintenance shutdown, a refinery manager said.
The 37,000 bpd crude distillation unit would be the first to return to service, followed by a 9,000 bpd cat cracker, a 7,000 bpd visbreaker, a 5,000 bpd desulfurization unit and a 3,000 bpd reformer.

The manager said the refinery, which is owned by state oil company ANCAP, had enough crude to run for more than a month, but would then resume its regular purchases of between 600,000 and one million barrels every 20 days.
ANCAP has held two product tenders to cover the refinery work.
